To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
iodine binds more strongly to waxy starches, starch granules with high surface area-to-volume ratios and starches with porous granule structures.

starch granule architecture, including the amylose content, particle density, particle size, and surface area, are all important in determining the amount of iodine that will be bound by starches exposed to iodine vapors equilibrated at various water activities.
iodine vapor binds to the surface of starch granules in proportion to the amylose content of the starch, the density of the granules and the surface area of the granules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quantification of total iodines in intact granular starchy materials.
the quantification of total iodin in intact starches of various botanical origin exposed to different water activity and the relationship of iodine binding and the structure of the granules.
the quantification of total iodinization of granular starches at different moisture contents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
starch granule architecture is important in determining the amount of iodine that is bound within the starch.
the iodine binding capacity of a starch is dependent upon the starch's amylose content, the surface area of the starch granules, and to a lesser extent, the density of the granules.

the more iodine that is bound to starch granules the more water soluble amylose is present in the starch, the more extensive the pores and channels are in the granule surface and the larger the starch granule surface area-to-volume is.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the starch granule is a complex structure with a variety of pores, channels, and surface areas that can be accessed and bound to iodine depending on starch composition, water activity and granule size.
starch granule architecture, amylose content, surface area-to-volume ratios and pore size are important factors that determine how iodine binds to starches of different origin.
the amount of iodine that is bound to starch granules is a reflection of both the starch granule structure and the amylose content of the starch.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the iodine binding is a dynamic process and the iodine binding capacity of starches depends on a complex interplay of factors such as amylose content, starch particle size and density, and the presence of surface pores and channels.
starch granule size and pore structure are important factors that affect how much iodine is bound within intact starches.

iodine vapor equilibriated to different water activities binds to starch granules and the level of iodine binding is affected by amylose content, surface area-to-volume ratios, and the presence of surface pores.
